summary: 'Can you help me' is HELP moving toward you (help-me) with a questioning face, or CAN YOU HELP-ME. The direction of HELP carries the 'me.'
steps: Sign HELP: rest a fist (thumb up) on your flat non-dominant palm.
Move the whole unit toward your own chest. HELP moving toward you means 'help me.'
Raise your eyebrows to make it a question. Add CAN (two fists dropping down) before it for the full sentence.
note: HELP is a directional verb. Moving it toward someone means 'help you'; moving it toward yourself means 'help me.' One sign, both meanings.
mistakes: Moving HELP away from yourself. That's 'I help you.'
